chapter_title: Chương 139: Thiếu Nữ Gió Ngâm, Chuông Phượng Từ Xa

segments.title: Chương 139: Thiếu Nữ Gió Ngâm, Chuông Phượng Từ Xa
segments.content:
Chapter 142-0139: A Maiden Named Fengyin, Phoenix Bells Ring Afar. An extra chapter for Alliance Leader Feng Sheng Shui Qi.

Chen Guiliang passed all six of his makeup exams, and every single one was a borderline pass.

The professors had been very generous.

He could muddle through the first semester of his freshman year like this, but the second semester wouldn't be so easy. If he failed too many courses then, he wouldn't even get a chance to take makeup exams; it would directly trigger a transfer to another department or force him to repeat the year.

Chen Guiliang made several calls, going through a few people before he finally contacted Peng Fei, the person Senior Kong had recommended.

This guy wasn't even in Beijing; he had just worked there for a project last year. Peng Fei was currently settled in Shanghai, making a living by composing music for soundtracks, and occasionally taking on other gigs.

As for song arrangement, he had only ever participated as a junior member, for example, being responsible for the string section of *The Legend of Mir*.

Peng Fei had no experience arranging an entire song by himself.

It wasn't that he didn't want to, but no one had given him the chance.

"Hello, Mr. Peng. I'm Chen Guiliang, the boss of ByteDance."

"Hello."

Peng Fei felt the name "Chen Guiliang" was a bit familiar, but he couldn't recall what he did.

Chen Guiliang said: "I'd like to hire you to arrange a song."

"Arrange a song?" Peng Fei's tone was slightly excited. "Will I be independently in charge, or assisting someone?"

Chen Guiliang said: "You'll be independently in charge. But as for the fee..."

Peng Fei quickly said: "A flat rate of 5000 yuan. I'm available whenever you need me."

He had proactively lowered his price.

At this time, hiring an amateur arranger or a student would cost between 1000 and 5000 yuan. For someone slightly more professional, the arrangement fee would be over 5000 yuan.

For example, the arrangement fee for *Mouse Loves Rice* was just over 2000 yuan.

For Peng Fei, making money was secondary; he wanted to be independently in charge of an arrangement!

Chen Guiliang said: "How about this: I'll give you 8000 yuan, and you'll also handle the post-production and recording. I'll cover your round-trip airfare, but you'll have to pay for your own room and board. You'll need to fly to Beijing."

"Do you have the lyrics, music, and a singer?" Peng Fei asked.

Chen Guiliang said: "They're all ready."

"I'll come over this weekend. Text me the address," Peng Fei agreed in an instant.

He didn't even ask what kind of song it was. He would take it even if it were an internet song, just to take that first step from 0 to 1 in his arrangement career.

Chen Guiliang was unfamiliar with the music industry and had no idea that the person he just hired would become a frequent winner of "Best Music" at domestic film festivals. He was also the one who arranged songs like Huo Zun's *Rolling up the Beaded Curtain* and often served as the music director for various music variety shows.

Of course, Peng Fei also had no idea how awesome he would be in the future.

Chen Guiliang walked into the company. The new employees hired last weekend were all secretly sizing him up.

Seeing Chen Guiliang approach, one of them quickly stood up and greeted him, "Hello, President Chen!"

"Hello."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "You don't need to stand up in the future. Just carry on with your work."

"Thank you, President Chen." The employee quickly sat back down.

Chen Guiliang walked straight up behind Xie Yang. "What are you looking at?"

Xie Yang pointed at the NGA forums and said: "Registration for the *World of Warcraft* closed beta opened today. The NGA forums have exploded. It's all posts about how to fill out the survey."

"You want to play too?" Chen Guiliang asked with a smile.

Xie Yang chuckled twice. "I do want to play. But I'm too lazy to sign up for the closed beta. I'll wait until open registration to play."

Chen Guiliang asked: "Has *World of Warcraft* captured all the attention on the major gaming forums?"

"It hasn't captured *all* of it, but posts related to *World of Warcraft* are definitely the most numerous," Xie Yang said. "The popularity of our Sanguosha and Xiaonei Wang is still climbing, with almost no negative feedback. 5q Campus Net is getting flamed hard."

Chen Guiliang said: "Getting flamed hard means it actually has users, but their user experience is poor. The social ecosystem probably hasn't been built up properly. It's better than nobody commenting at all. That would mean users can't even be bothered to complain about them."

Xie Yang was taken aback, feeling that this made sense.

After Xiaonei Wang opened its registration, the number of users grew rapidly. The current registered user count has surpassed the 350,000 mark.

This was especially true for universities in Beijing. Due to the early natural spread, over 50% of students at many universities were Xiaonei Wang users. This figure had already surpassed the percentage of students who owned a computer.

To support so many users, Chen Guiliang had now switched to leasing servers, with monthly costs as high as 65,000 yuan. If the number of users continued to increase, the fees would have to go up too!

He had to find a way to monetize and recoup his costs.

But Xiaonei Wang couldn't have too many ads, or it would annoy the users. The ad content also had to be selective. Chen Guiliang would never accept ads for things like pharmaceuticals or health supplements.

Fortunately, he still had Sanguosha bringing in money.

The online version of Sanguosha currently had 476,000 registered users and 218,000 daily active users. In the 38 days since the payment function was enabled, the total amount recharged was 752,000 yuan.

As for the physical Sanguosha card game, there were currently over 6,000 online stores selling it on consignment. Most of these stores hadn't sold a single set.

However, the effect was still very obvious. The highest daily sales had now reached over 320 sets. Even if he only made a few yuan per set, that was still about 50,000 yuan in profit a month.

He still had to rely on Sanguosha.

At this rate, the Sanguosha online game could probably break into the top 10 by the end of the year!

China's online game market today was long past what it was like when Chen Guiliang and Tao Chenggang were running private servers.

On last year's annual online game rankings, *Ragnarok Online* had charged to first place, *MU Online* to second, and *Westward Journey Online II* was third.

*The Legend of Mir* had dropped to sixth, and *The World of Legend* had dropped to tenth.

*The Legend of Mir 3*, which was once on the verge of being ruined by its operator, had magically made a comeback to eighth place.

Only two months had passed this year, and *Jian Xia Qing Yuan Online 2* had shot to first on the monthly charts, while *The World of Legend* had soared from tenth straight back to second.

"Knock, knock, knock..."

A girl wearing a hat and carrying a backpack stood at the entrance, timidly knocking on the company's open door.

"Excuse me, is this Game Science?"

"Come in. What are you here for?"

"President Chen told me to come to work. My name is Xu Fengyin."

"President Chen is next door, at the ByteDance office."

"Oh, thank you."

Xu Fengyin, looking like a thief, scurried over to the office next door. "Excuse me, is President Chen here?"

"Go further inside, by the window..."

A new employee who had just started this week looked up as he spoke and was stunned by the girl's beauty.

"Thank you."

Xu Fengyin walked without a sound, as if she had practiced some kind of lightness skill.

"Hello, President Chen, I'm Tiandao Qian," Xu Fengyin said.

Chen Guiliang jumped, not having sensed anyone beside him at all. He then smiled, stood up, and shook her hand. "Welcome, welcome. Our lead artist has finally arrived. Come on, I'll take you to see our grand steward to handle the onboarding."

Walking over to Ao Yanchen's desk, Chen Guiliang introduced her: "This is Tiandao Qian... uh, what's your real name?"

Xu Fengyin said: "Xu Fengyin. Xu as in 'permit,' Feng as in 'wind,' and Yin as in 'chant.'"

Chen Guiliang said: "Right, Xu Fengyin. A top student from the Academy of Fine Arts. The best-selling Sanguo Show skins and general skins were all drawn by her."

"Welcome, welcome!" Ao Yanchen was overjoyed.

"Do I process my onboarding here?"

Xu Fengyin opened her backpack and took out a pile of things: student ID, ID card, award certificates, a school internship recommendation letter, and more.

"Thud!"

As she took out her things, a manga fell onto the floor.

Xu Fengyin hastily bent down to pick it up, then quickly stuffed it back into her backpack.

In that fleeting moment, Chen Guiliang saw clearly that the cover of the manga seemed a bit risqué.

Ao Yanchen had her fill out a form, then go make copies of her ID and student ID.

Xu Fengyin went to make copies with her head down, not daring to meet Chen Guiliang's gaze again.

She was mortified, to the point she almost didn't want to work here anymore. Her secret had been discovered by the boss on her very first day.

Ao Yanchen said teasingly, "President Chen, this girl is quite pretty."

Chen Guiliang rolled his eyes. "Am I that kind of person?"

"Hard to say," Ao Yanchen retorted, then asked, "How much are we paying her?"

Chen Guiliang said: "It's already been settled. 3000 a month."

At major companies like Shanda and NetEase, the monthly salary for a junior artist at this time was 3500-5000. Senior artists could earn nearly 10,000 a month!

Of course, small companies definitely couldn't offer that much; some were so broke they only paid 2000.

Xu Fengyin returned with the copies of her documents and signed the labor contract with her head bowed.

Ao Yanchen then said: "Write down the specific configuration for the kind of computer you need."

"Oh." Xu Fengyin picked up a pen to write, her peripheral vision fixed on the shoes next to her.

They were Chen Guiliang's shoes. Xu Fengyin wished her boss would get lost already.

But Chen Guiliang stood right there chatting with Senior Ao, discussing business development for Xiaonei Wang.

Ao Yanchen said: "I think three ad slots on the homepage are enough. One banner at the top, and two vertical ones on the sides. Let's test the users' reaction first, then slowly add more later. As for pricing, I'll research other websites first."

How would she research?

By calling them one by one, of course, claiming to be a client, asking for prices while also inquiring about data like their ad traffic.

Chen Guiliang said: "Just three ad slots. We don't need to hire anyone new for that, right?"

Ao Yanchen said irritably: "Just say what you mean. I can handle sales part-time!"

"Haha."

Chen Guiliang gave an awkward laugh, and finally left, satisfied.

"Phew..."

Xu Fengyin let out a long sigh of relief in her heart.

Ao Yanchen stamped the labor contract and said to Xu Fengyin: "You can choose your own desk. But don't pick one in this office; you're an employee of Game Science next door."

"Thank you." Xu Fengyin quickly made her escape.

"Wait a minute!" Ao Yanchen called out.

Xu Fengyin hurriedly ran back.

Ao Yanchen asked: "Do you have a place to live?"

Xu Fengyin said: "I haven't found one yet."

Ao Yanchen said: "The employees who joined last year are all living in Changchun Xinyuan. But no new people can move in there this year. New employees are renting places over in Yandong Yuan, and the company provides a monthly housing subsidy. Yandong Yuan is an old faculty housing building for Peking University. The living conditions are a bit poor, but you can go have a look."

"Okay."

"You don't have to come to the company tomorrow. You can go rent a place and buy daily necessities first."

"Thank you."

Xu Fengyin vanished in a flash, not even choosing a desk, and bolted all the way to the elevator.

Only when she was outside the building did she remember that she didn't know where Yandong Yuan was, so she began the slow process of asking for directions to find a place to live.

(End of this chapter)
